title: Introduce lightweight sieve test runner, minimal dep-lock, and release quiet-gate
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Our full integration suites are growing expensive and brittle; several recent release blocks were caused by transient infra flakes and dependency drift. This PR introduces a lightweight "sieve" test runner for fast preflight filtering of obvious regressions, adds a minimal dep-lock script to pin transitive versions for CI lanes, and wires a temporary release quiet-gate so that release automation waits for the sieve lane to stabilize before promoting artifacts.

What this change does (single continuous description): Adds a new lightweight test harness (tools/sieve-runner) that executes a prioritized subset of integration scenarios with short timeouts and deterministic environment knobs; updates the CI workflow to run the sieve lane in parallel to unit tests and only mark the preflight step green when the sieve lane has passed twice within a 30-minute window; introduces tools/dep-pin.py which scans lockfiles and generates a minimal transitive pin manifest (ci/transitive-pins.txt) used by the sieve lane to reduce flakiness caused by upstream micro-version churn; provides a developer-facing make target (make sieve-local) and VS Code task for reproducing failed sieve runs locally; documents the workflow and operational playbook in docs/ci/sieve-playbook.md; and gates release.yml with a quiet-window check to avoid promotions during transient CI instability.

Checklist: - [x] Add sieve runner and CI integration - [x] Add dep-pin script and initial transitive pin manifest - [x] Add local run instructions and VS Code task - [x] Update CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml - [x] Add playbook and runbook entries - [x] Smoke-tested on staging CI lane

Related: ENG-3214 tracks reducing release flakiness; ENG-3301 documents the dep pinning strategy. This is intentionally conservative: sieve runner is opt-in for a short period and only influences the release quiet gate; it does not remove long-running integration lanes.

review_thread: Ethan Park: Nice approach. Can you add a metric export point so we can graph sieve pass/fail counts historically? Also please ensure the sieve uses the same env stamping as full integration so failures are comparable.

Maya Thompson: Added a Prometheus push endpoint and metric name prefix (sieve_) in runner.py; the playbook documents where the metric appears in the CI dashboard. The sieve uses CI_ENV and IMAGE_TAG from the same env pipeline variables as full integration; note there is an opt-in 'sieve_override' flag for local reproductions.
Priya Nair: The dep-pin script looks useful, but please avoid shipping a full lockfile in the repo. Can the script emit only transient pins used by sieve lane?

Maya Thompson: It emits a 'transitive-pins.txt' that only lists packages observed in the sieve lane runtime graph (about ~45 entries); this is committed as a short-lived artifact to stabilize the alpha lane and will be rotated by the dep-pin workflow. I've added a comment in the file header to indicate intended rotation cadence.
Luis Ortega: CI changes look ok; two small asks: add a short-circuit to skip sieve on feature branches with label 'no-sieve' and add a 2nd pass requirement before release for extra safety.
Maya Thompson: Implemented both: ci.yml checks for labels via GitHub context and the release job requires the sieve lane to have two consecutive successful runs (state kept in CI annotations).
Ethan Park: Approving after verifying metrics surfaced in dashboard and second-pass logic. Priya: approved. Luis: approved.
